plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 25% to favor income.
Trim QQQ to 15% and SMH to 5% to further reduce concentration.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Reduce QQQ to 15% and SMH to 5% to diversify.
Maintain small allocations to SOXL (3%) and SPAL (2%) for limited leverage.
Buy AAPL at 4% to add a high-quality name with a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances growth with risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall concentration and leverage while introducing a high-quality new name. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a balanced approach to upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Reduce QQQ to 10% and SMH to 5% to free up capital.
Add to SOXL (6%) and SPAL (6%) to increase leveraged exposure.
Buy AAPL at 6% to add a high-quality name with a strong scanner setup.
This plan leans into leverage and high-scoring setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach amplifies both upside and drawdown, and leveraged ETFs decay daily. Strict stop discipline is critical to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% to prioritize income.
Trim QQQ to 10% and SMH to 5% to reduce growth and high-beta exposure.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates heavily into income-generating ETFs and broad index, cutting high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
